title: Definite Articles in Nominative
sourceNote: The auto-captions are garbled in several places (some example sentences could not be reconstructed). The explanation of the nominative case and the table of definite articles are clear; extra nouns and examples are marked as supplementary.
objectives: I can explain what the nominative case and the subject are
I can use der, die, das and plural die
I know that every German noun has an article and starts with a capital letter
I can find the nominative with the questions Wer? and Was?

patterns.ex: Wer ist das? – Das ist Peter.
patterns.en: Who is that? – That is Peter.

patterns.form: Was ist das? – Das ist + [article + noun].
patterns.ex: Was ist das? – Das ist das Haus.
patterns.en: What is that? – That is the house.

grammar.title: What is the nominative?
grammar.body:
A sentence is made of a **subject** and a **verb**. The subject is always in the **nominative case**, and the verb is conjugated to match the subject.

The subject can be a **noun** (Nomen / Substantiv) or a **pronoun** (ich, du, er ... – see lesson 11). A noun can be a person or a thing, singular or plural.

grammar.title: Find the nominative with Wer? and Was?
grammar.body: Ask **Wer?** (who) for a person and **Was?** (what) for a thing. The answer is the nominative.

examples.de: Wer ist das? – Das ist Peter.
examples.en: Who is that? – That is Peter.

examples.de: Was ist das? – Das ist das Haus.
examples.en: What is that? – That is the house.

grammar.title: Every noun has an article and a capital letter
grammar.body:
In German **all nouns** have an article that stands before them, and **all nouns** start with a **capital letter** – common nouns and proper nouns alike.

There are three kinds of articles: the **definite** article (bestimmter Artikel: *the*), the **indefinite** article (unbestimmter Artikel: *a*) and the negative article (*kein*, *no*). In this lesson we only study the definite article in the nominative.
grammar.ar: كل اسم في الألمانية له أداة ويبدأ بحرف كبير.

grammar.title: The definite articles (nominative)
grammar.body:
There are three genders in the singular: **masculine (der)**, **feminine (die)** and **neuter (das)**. In the plural the article is always **die**, whatever the gender – it looks like the feminine one.

Tip: learn every noun with its article. A simple way to remember: write **m** for *der*, **f** for *die* and **n** for *das*.
grammar.ar: المذكّر der، المؤنّث die، المحايد das، والجمع دائمًا die.

mistakes.why: In the plural the article is always *die*.
All German nouns start with a capital letter.

pronunciation.tip: *ie* is a long 'ee': *die*, *vier*. But *ei* sounds like 'eye': *Wein*, *klein*.

lines.de: Das ist Peter. Der Mann ist groß.
lines.en: That is Peter. The man is tall.

lines.de: Das ist das Haus. Das Haus ist groß.
lines.en: That is the house. The house is big.

tip: Learn every noun together with its article, for example der Mann, die Frau, das Kind – never the noun alone.
